tag: Sprint 14 Task E, F117 (F114 cloud read)

define-linear-quadratic-order: Section 'Linear and quadratic terms': the paper defines order as the maximum number of terms multiplied together and names single terms linear and pairwise products quadratic.
define-lubo: Section 'Linear and quadratic terms': LUBO is introduced and defined in the text as a QUBO-like problem with 0/1 variables, with a worked example.
cnf-definition: Section 'Satisfiability': the paper states that problems are conventionally written in CNF and then defines CNF (conjunctive clauses using OR and NOT) with an example.
hamming-74-setup: Section 'Decoding of Error Correction': the paper states that it takes the Hamming [7,4] code as its example. The correction property is the paper's description of that code.
hamming-74-parity-definitions: Section 'Decoding of Error Correction': the paper defines p1, p2, p3 as mod-2 sums and states the decoding task, as the setup of the example.
linear-operations-definition: Section 'Linear operations and tensors': the page defines linear operations (adding and subtracting, possibly weighted) and states that sets of linear equations are represented as matrices.
linear-model-superposition-definition: Section 'Nonlinearity as a high-level concept': the lesson defines linearity of a model through the superposition property of its solutions.
nonlinearity-is-mathematical-property: Section 'Nonlinearity as a high-level concept': the page states how it uses the term (a property of the mathematical model) and says that calling a system 'nonlinear' is only shorthand. This is its own terminology.
nonlinear-optics-definition: Opening paragraph: the page defines nonlinear optics as the study of light-matter effects that depend on intensity and are nonlinear in the field strength.
linear-optics-definition: Section 'Linear and nonlinear optics': the page defines linear optics as the regime well approximated as linear in the fields. The second clause restates what a linear model implies.
qci-optics-q-factor-definition: Section 'Non-linear optics': the page defines the Q-factor as the measure that determines how many round trips light makes before being lost.
qci-optics-scope-high-level-overview: Opening paragraph and 'Further reading': the page says it is a high-level overview, keeps the explanation conceptual and gives no full mathematical explanation.
qci-qudit-definition: Introduction to Qudits in EQC, first paragraph: qudits are defined as units of quantum information taking more than two states.
qci-qudit-scope-feedback-eqc-analog: Introduction to Qudits in EQC: the page states it will not go into the details of EQC and will discuss a qudit in feedback-based, analog EQC.
qci-qudit-quantum-die-state: Section 'Superposition': the page writes the state of its quantum die example as a sum of six amplitudes times kets. This is the example's own notation.
qci-qudit-decoding-definition: Section 'Computation': the page names the translation of measurements to the problem domain 'decoding' and gives discrete and continuous examples.
qci-qudit-dimensionality-solution-vector: Section 'Qudit Dimensionality': the page defines how n qudits of dimensionality k map to a solution vector of size n with k values per element. The 'most common measure' remark is incidental.
qci-qudit-conclusion-summary: Conclusion: the page states what the primer covered.

theory_low.unconstrained-linear-is-easy: The one-line minimization argument is informal, and the value also carries the authors' opinion that such models are 'not very interesting'. Not a stated and proved theorem.
theory_low.qubo-frustration-example: An illustrative example with an informal explanation of frustration, and the authors' claim that it makes a general QUBO non-trivial. Not a theorem with a proof.
theory_low.qubo-minimum-value-example: A worked example stated without derivation (minimum -1 at x1=x2=x3=1, which checks by hand). Illustration, not a stated and proved result. The quote is also mojibake from the text layer.
theory_low.sat-to-polynomial-encoding: A constructive description with one example, in a vendor lesson. Not a stated theorem and no proof of equivalence.
theory_low.sat-order-equals-clause-width: Stated as 'clearly' after one example. An informal observation with no proof.
theory_low.factoring-objective-fourth-order: Section 'Factoring': the objective (X1X2-N)^2 is given and the fourth-order remark is asserted informally. An authors' construction, not a proved result.
theory_low.factoring-six-binary-example: A worked toy example the authors say is 'relatively straightforward to check'. The text even has an index typo (x2(3)). Not run or proved. Illustration only.
theory_low.factoring-binary-needs-fourth-order: The 'most direct way' conclusion is the authors' interpretation drawn from one example, with no proof that fourth-order terms are needed.
theory_low.ising-parity-product: The identity follows from the stated mapping z=2(1/2-x), but the paper only says 'we can see'. It is not a stated and proved result, and the first quote is the authors' opinion on what is most natural.
theory_low.decoding-is-multibody: The authors' own interpretation ('fundamentally a multi-body problem'), not a proved result.
theory_low.hamming-74-energy-function: The energy function is the authors' construction, given with no derivation or proof that its minimum decodes the code.
theory_low.hamming-74-single-error-argument: An informal argument 'by inspecting this formula', not a proof. It covers only the single-error case and is the authors' interpretation.
theory_low.derivative-linear-operation: The page gives a short sketch from the limit definition. This is not a stated and proved theorem, and it is not a definition, so the suggested basis does not fit. It is an informal calculus argument.
theory_low.linear-ode-criterion: A rule stated as a consequence of the derivative sketch, without a proof or full conditions. Informal.
theory_low.one-nonlinear-term-suffices: A bare rule stated without proof, in a lesson. It is not a definition: the page defines linearity through superposition, and this follows only informally.
theory_low.qci-qudit-can-be-constrained-to-qubit: Section 'Doing What Qubits Can Do Plus More': a short sketch in a vendor primer that assumes integer-valued X, with no statement of conditions and no proof.
theory_low.qci-qudit-penalty-term-qubo: A sketched penalty construction with no bound on lambda and no proof. The page also says its hardware uses a different approach in practice.
theory_low.qci-qudit-worked-example-quadratic: A worked arithmetic example (f(99,0) = -19602 checks) in a vendor primer, not a stated and proved result and not run on a device.
